name: CoStar Group

logo.source: Wikidata logo property for CoStar Group (CoStar Group logo.svg on Commons)

description: CoStar owns no property; it sells information and advertising to people who do. Its commercial segment (CoStar database, LoopNet listings, Matterport 3D scans, lease software) charges subscription fees; its residential segment (Apartments.com, Homes.com, Land.com, plus Domain in Australia and OnTheMarket in the UK) charges property managers and agents for listings and leads. Revenue was $3.25B in 2025 (+19 percent), 55 percent commercial and 45 percent residential. Commercial earns a 38 percent adjusted EBITDA margin; residential lost $230M of adjusted EBITDA in 2025 because of heavy Homes.com marketing and sales spending, though it turned slightly positive in Q2 2026 ($12M).

gics.note: Sector and sub-industry per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies'. Mowgli note: it owns no property; revenue is monthly or annual subscription and advertising fees from real estate professionals, so it behaves like a data and online-marketplace software company.

hq.note: 1201 Wilson Blvd (SEC EDGAR business address); Wikipedia's S&P 500 list shows Washington, D.C.; see conflicts

employees.note: 10-K says 'over 8,000 employees in 20 countries'; exact figure not given

businessLines.name: Commercial Real Estate
businessLines.how: Fixed monthly or annual subscription fees, set by number of sites, users and client size, on contracts mostly of a year or more that renew automatically; LoopNet charges owners and brokers per paid listing; Matterport sells subscriptions plus capture services and devices.
businessLines.description: CoStar (commercial property database: properties, leasing, sales comps, tenants, owners, markets, STR hotel benchmarking, debt tools), LoopNet network (commercial listings), Matterport 3D digital twins (acquired February 28, 2025), and lease management SaaS (CoStar Real Estate Manager, Visual Lease).

revenue.note: FY2024 $1,515M (+18%). CoStar $1,259M (39% of total; +9%); LoopNet $312M (10%; +11%); Other Commercial $216M (7%; includes $147M of Matterport). Six months to 2026-06-30: $953M vs $855M.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $1,515M (+18%). CoStar $1,259M (39% of total; +9%); LoopNet $312M (10%; +11%); Other Commercial $216M (7%; includes $147M of Matterport). Six months to 2026-06-30: $953M vs $855M.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $602M. Residential segment was -$230M, so the two sum to $442M; a profit share is not meaningful. Margin computed. Six months to 2026-06-30 adjusted EBITDA $333M vs $312M.

businessLines.name: Residential Real Estate
businessLines.how: Property managers pay a monthly fee to advertise apartments on Apartments.com; agents pay for advertising and leads on Homes.com on a 'your listing, your lead' basis; Domain and OnTheMarket charge agents for listings. Spending on marketing (mostly for Homes.com) is the main cost.
businessLines.description: Apartments.com network (ApartmentFinder, ForRent.com and others), Homes.com, Land.com, Domain (Australia, acquired August 27, 2025) and OnTheMarket (UK, acquired December 2023).

revenue.note: FY2024 $1,221M (+20%), including $95M from Domain. Six months to 2026-06-30: $869M vs $658M. No sub-split of Apartments.com versus Homes.com revenue was found in the filings read.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $1,221M (+20%), including $95M from Domain. Six months to 2026-06-30: $869M vs $658M. No sub-split of Apartments.com versus Homes.com revenue was found in the filings read.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 -$361M. Q2 2026 +$12M vs -$76M; six months to 2026-06-30 -$17M vs -$161M. Margin computed.

brands.share: $147M of revenue after the February 28, 2025 acquisition (inside Other Commercial $216M)

brands.share: Not split out; Residential total $1,460M, 45% of revenue

brands.share: $95M of 2025 revenue since the August 27, 2025 acquisition (plus $6M of commercial listings in LoopNet)
